description:
About the Position

The University of Essex recruits a Doctoral Research Fellow in the Department of Government within the DIViNE MSCA Doctoral Network on political violence and democracy. The fellow will pursue doctoral research on political violence, institutional reform and democratic resilience, contributing to the network's comparative research programme. Essex's Department of Government is one of the UK's leading political science departments, with long-standing research strengths in conflict, democracy and political behaviour.

The appointment carries a salary of GBP 38,784 - GBP 46,049 per annum, reflecting the MSCA doctoral candidate conditions, and includes network-level training, secondments and joint supervision across DIViNE partner institutions. The vacancy page lists a closing date of 11 November 2026, while the DIViNE network's application deadline is 15 November 2026, so candidates should prepare their materials early. The fellow will be based in Colchester with access to Essex's research centres and data resources.

Candidate Profile and Application Route

Applicants hold a strong master's degree in political science, government or a related social-science field, with demonstrated interest in political violence or democracy research and suitable quantitative or mixed-methods skills. MSCA mobility rules apply to doctoral candidates in the network, so applicants must not have resided or carried out their main activity in the UK for more than 12 of the last 36 months. Applications are submitted through the University of Essex online recruitment system with a CV, transcripts, references and a research statement.

Highlights

  • MSCA DIViNE Doctoral Research Fellow position
  • Department of Government, a UK-leading political science unit
  • Political violence and democracy research programme
  • Salary GBP 38,784 - 46,049 per annum
  • Network training, secondments and joint supervision
  • Page deadline 11 November 2026; network deadline 15 November 2026

The University of Essex is a public research university in Colchester, England, with additional campuses in Southend and Loughton. Its Department of Government is ranked among the strongest in the UK, and the university is internationally known for research on conflict, human rights, democracy and the social sciences. Doctoral researchers join an international academic community with dedicated graduate training and funding support.
